version.changelog:
Initial release: Easily publish videos and photo carousels to TikTok via the Boring platform.

- Supports direct video or photo carousel posting to TikTok, including captions and privacy settings.
- Draft mode available: send content to TikTok inbox for manual publishing.
- Requires no local API keys—authentication handled via the MCP connector link.
- Handles media upload (video/photos) and provides clear error reporting.
- Step-by-step workflow and security guidance included.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: tiktok-publisher
Version: 1.0.0

The skill facilitates TikTok publishing by routing local media through a third-party service (boring.aiagent-me.com) and uploading files to Google Cloud Storage. It utilizes an MCP Connector link that contains an embedded authentication token directly in the URL, which is a risky credential management practice. While these behaviors are documented and aligned with the stated purpose of the skill, the requirement to transmit local files to an intermediary service and the use of sensitive tokens in URLs constitute high-risk capabilities (SKILL.md).

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, required credential (a Boring MCP connector link) and actions align with a TikTok publishing purpose, but the connector token is a sensitive third‑party credential and the skill's source is external — verify trust and token scope before use.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (publish videos/carousels to TikTok) match the runtime instructions: listing TikTok accounts, uploading media, and calling boring_publish_post. Requiring an MCP connector link to Boring (which holds the OAuth token to TikTok) is coherent with the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to call boring_list_accounts, boring_upload_file/boring_upload_from_url, and boring_publish_post. It also notes media is uploaded to Boring's Google Cloud Storage and that the MCP link contains an embedded auth token. These steps stay within the publishing workflow, but they involve sending user media and publish commands through a third party (Boring). The instructions assume connector functions exist; they do not ask the agent to read unrelated local files or other system secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code to download and run. That minimizes filesystem/install risk. The homepage and documentation are hosted on boring-doc.aiagent-me.com (external); the skill's source is listed as unknown, so confirm the external service identity before trusting it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or local secrets are requested. Instead the skill requires an MCP Connector link (a URL with an embedded auth token). That is proportional to its purpose but is a high‑value credential: the link functions like a password and likely grants Boring the ability to act on your behalf (including publishing and accessing media). The SKILL.md does not enumerate least‑privilege scopes for the MCP token, so confirm what the connector can do.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and autonomous invocation is allowed (default). The skill does not request permanent agent-level presence or modify other skills. There is no install-time persistence or system configuration modification.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says, but it relies on you pasting a Boring 'MCP link' that contains an embedded auth token. Treat that link like a password: only provide it if you trust boring.aiagent-me.com and understand what actions the connector can perform. Before installing: (1) verify the external service's identity and privacy/storage policies (media will be uploaded to Boring's Google Cloud Storage); (2) confirm the connector's OAuth scopes and that they are limited to TikTok publishing only; (3) test with non-sensitive content; (4) be prepared to revoke/regenerate the MCP token if you stop using the skill or suspect misuse. If you cannot verify the third‑party service or need stricter control over credentials, do not install or use this skill.
